chapter: Old New Orleans bands and Buddy Bolden
title: Instrumentation of the Bolden band and its players
summary: Tio describes the seven-piece string-style band with violin leader, cornet, trombone, clarinet, guitar, bass and drummers, naming Bob Lyons, Frankie Dusen and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I interrupted when you were talking about Buddy Bolden for a minute was there anything else you really had?
I'd like to ask... I'd like to try and find out how the band sounded did they sound like any band today or how many pieces were in there?
Well in them days the Portland band was a seven piece band
That would be a string band?

That would be a string band. Well you used to use the violin you know, violin is a leader, you used to use the violin as a leader and you had your cornet, a very youth trumpet at that time. It was cornet, there was trombone, clarinet, guitar, then later on came in the banjo. And the guitar was full. Buddy Manatee played. Those old guys hanging around Renfort Street, he played bass. They had a bass? Bob Lyons maybe? Bob Lyons. Bob Lyons. They played bass and also guitar. I knew him. Would they have a drummer in those venues? Oh yeah, they had a lot of drummers. Luke Watrell was one of them and they had a bunch of them. Oh yeah. Is there the Singleton? He's in Chicago now. I think so. Yeah. The Bolin band would have a drummer with them, of course. Oh yeah. Yeah, they had a drummer. Yeah, I don't remember who the drummer was. I know one trombone player was Franky Dooson. Yeah. I remember Franky Dooson. You remember Franky Dooson? Franky Dooson was a trombone player. Big drummer. Yeah, tall.
